name: ppm
shortDescription: Parts per million — the standard concentration unit for pool chemistry.
longDescription: 1 ppm = 1 mg/L = 1 part chemical per 1,000,000 parts water. Used for free chlorine, combined chlorine, alkalinity, calcium hardness, CYA, TDS, salt, metals, and phosphates.

name: mg/L
shortDescription: Milligrams per liter — numerically identical to ppm in aqueous solutions.
longDescription: In dilute aqueous solutions (including pool water), mg/L and ppm are numerically equal: 1 mg/L = 1 ppm. mg/L is the SI unit preferred in scientific contexts, while ppm is the practical shorthand used in pool industry applications.

name: US Gallons
shortDescription: US liquid gallon — the primary volume unit for pool calculations in North America.
longDescription: 1 US gallon = 3.785 liters = 0.1337 cubic feet. Pool volume in gallons is used in every chemical dose calculation. 7.48 gallons per cubic foot is the standard conversion used in pool volume formulas.

name: Liters
shortDescription: SI unit of volume. 1 US gallon = 3.785 liters.
longDescription: 1 liter = 0.2642 US gallons = 1,000 milliliters. Used in metric countries for pool volume measurement. Chemical concentrations in mg/L are equivalent to ppm.

name: °F
shortDescription: Degrees Fahrenheit — the standard temperature unit for pool and spa temperature in North America.
longDescription: Fahrenheit is the US standard for temperature measurement. Pool temperature targets: 78–84°F (residential pools), 100–104°F maximum (hot tubs). LSI temperature factor tables use °F. Conversion: °C = (°F − 32) × 5/9.

name: °C
shortDescription: Degrees Celsius — the SI temperature unit used in metric countries.
longDescription: Celsius is the SI standard for temperature. Pool targets: 25–29°C (residential), maximum 40°C (hot tubs). Conversion: °F = °C × 9/5 + 32.

name: Minutes
shortDescription: Unit of time — used for pump turnover calculation and wait times after chemical additions.
longDescription: Minutes are used in pool chemistry for: turnover rate calculations (Volume in gallons / GPM = turnover time in minutes), wait times after chemical additions, and filtration cycle timing.

name: Hours
shortDescription: Unit of time — used for turnover rate and pump run time calculations.
longDescription: Hours are the standard unit for expressing pool turnover time, pump daily run time, and wait times for chemical balancing. PHTA recommends a maximum 8-hour turnover time for residential pools.

name: Days
shortDescription: Unit of time — used for maintenance scheduling and chemical activity timelines.
longDescription: Days are used for maintenance scheduling (test twice per week, shock weekly), CYA dissolution time (24–48 days), water change intervals for hot tubs (every 90 days), and chemical activity timelines.

name: Weeks
shortDescription: Unit of time — used for maintenance scheduling (weekly testing, weekly shock).
longDescription: Weeks are the standard interval for pool maintenance activities: weekly water testing, weekly shock treatment (optional), weekly brushing and vacuuming, and weekly filter checks.

name: Months
shortDescription: Unit of time — used for seasonal maintenance intervals and hot tub water change schedules.
longDescription: Monthly intervals are used for: calcium hardness and CYA testing (monthly), hot tub water changes (every 3–4 months), filter inspection, and salt level verification.
